papers.summary: S-SALAAD learns low-rank and structured-sparse weight components during training to support compression of one checkpoint to several budgets. Its low-rank-only ablation compares ADMM-based structure learning with direct nuclear-norm regularization.
papers.relevance: Closest match to training for low-rank compressibility while preserving quality. Reported efficiency gains concern inference, not training memory.

evidence.quote: jointly learns the model weights and their low-rank and structured sparse components during training
L L -only S-SALAAD maintains low perplexity over the same budget range, providing a better trade-off between model quality and elastic compressibility than these direct regularization baselines.

papers.title: Learning Structured Sparsity for Large Models: Bridging Model Compressibility and Efficient Inference

papers.summary: LEMS allocates SVD ranks using layer-wise error modeling; KFAC-SVD addresses decomposition quality. The paper reports compression results across several LLM families and sizes.
papers.relevance: Directly informs low-rank LLM compression, rank allocation, and quality-versus-budget decisions.

evidence.quote: Table 2 details the results for all approaches under uniform compression rates (0.9, 0.7) and calibration sample count
Averaged over ratios and models, it reduces perplexity by 17% for KFAC-SVD and 34% for SVD-LLM , while increasing zero-shot accuracy by +7.2 and +9.1 p.p.

papers.title: Advancing SVD-based LLM Compression via Layer-Wise Error Model Search

papers.summary: A controlled quadratic analysis identifies when Muon’s polar update helps or hurts. Finite Newton–Schulz iterations can outperform exact orthogonalization by softening updates along tiny singular directions.
papers.relevance: Connects matrix spectra and Newton–Schulz approximation to optimizer behavior, but its trajectory results rely on quadratics.

evidence.quote: compare update directions under line search to remove the effect of learning-rate tuning.
Finite Newton--Schulz softens the update exactly there and can then converge faster than exact polar, so it is not merely an approximation of the polar factor.

papers.title: A Quadratic Lens on Muon's Polar Update: Benefits, Pitfalls, and the Role of Newton-Schulz

papers.summary: Analyzes initialization-induced noise in LoRA with asymmetric learning rates and proposes a smaller-variance initialization to widen the stable learning-rate region.
papers.relevance: Addresses practical LoRA optimization and stability in LLM fine-tuning.

evidence.quote: Under matched rank and training time for both initializations, this reduces the initialization-noise energy by an additional factor of 1 / n
reduces best-ratio drift, prevents the high-ratio collapse observed with standard Init[A]

papers.title: Rethinking LoRA Initialization for Robust Asymmetric Learning Rates

papers.summary: An error-diffusion optimizer replaces full-precision latent weights with quantized residual buffers for binary-weight language-model training. Reported state savings exclude several full-precision components.
papers.relevance: A concrete memory–quality tradeoff for training, though tested models are far smaller than current LLMs.

evidence.quote: cuts the training state per weight from 97 bits to 3–9, up to 19 ×
The tasks are a synthetic MLP benchmark and language models with at most 19M parameters (70M with the wikitext-103 embeddings) and six layers on one GPU
Per-layer weight scales, per-batch activation scales, and the FP embeddings, LayerNorms, and head of the transformers are excluded from the per-weight count

papers.title: Error Diffusion Replaces Latent Weights: Training Binary-Weight Language Models on a Few Bits of Dithered State

papers.summary: Experiments compare test error and memorization under random labels across model sizes; a separate kernel-gradient-flow analysis gives regimes in which early stopping helps or interpolation is preferable.
papers.relevance: Direct match to generalization and memorization under label noise, with a clear limit on what the theory explains about deep networks.

evidence.quote: For the larger, deeper convolutional and residual networks, this deterioration is essentially absent: their best observed test performance is attained with zero memorization error
Our analysis does not, however, establish that the networks learn this same geometry

papers.title: When is early stopping beneficial under label noise? A phase diagram for kernel gradient flow

papers.summary: A controlled SciFact ablation compares closed-book, one-shot retrieval, ReAct-style query writing, and oracle abstracts. Query writing improves gold-paper recall, but accuracy differences among realistic harnesses are not significant in this pilot.
papers.relevance: Directly informs a handwritten literature-search harness, particularly query formulation and citation validation.

evidence.quote: We hold the backbone model, prompt format, and output schema fixed and vary only the harness
The agentic harness raises gold recall to 19–20% and attains the highest accuracy (62.0 for both backbones)
none of the accuracy differences between realistic harnesses is significant.

papers.title: Real PMIDs, Wrong Papers: Harness Design for Biomedical Claim-Verification Agents

limitations: S-SALAAD’s exact matched-budget numerical comparisons were not established by the retrieved passages; its reported latency results are for inference.
The binary-weight training study does not establish LLM-scale or wall-clock efficiency; its per-weight state count is not total training memory.
The SciFact harness study uses 100 claims per condition and two small backbones from one provider.
X analysis was disabled; no attention or popularity claim is made.
